subject.title: Feature: fire session-memory hook on session reset/prune, not just compaction

question: Should OpenClaw broaden session-memory or reset lifecycle hooks to automatic daily/idle rollover and maintenance prune, and which event contract should own that behavior?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent API affects plugin-visible lifecycle semantics, sensitive transcript retention, reset latency, and maintenance-prune timing, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Define a lifecycle contract first
options.body: Approve a bounded reset/prune memory-preservation contract, including payload, timeout, dedupe, retention, and security rules, before implementation.

options.title: Land the reset subset only
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 or a replacement for daily/idle rollover and keep maintenance prune as a separate product decision.

options.title: Keep persistence plugin-owned
options.body: Do not add core session-memory behavior now; ask memory plugins or external services to use existing lifecycle surfaces and only reopen for a concrete missing API.

recommendation.title: Define a lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Approve a bounded reset/prune memory-preservation contract, including payload, timeout, dedupe, retention, and security rules, before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across reset behavior, memory-flush policy, and recent lifecycle-hook product decisions.
